title: India surpasses China in FDI inflows
reason: The core claim does not hold on any standard/authoritative FDI-inflows measure. UNCTAD's World Investment Report 2025 (the internationally standard FDI benchmark, corroborated independently via insightsonindia.com's summary of it) puts India's 2024 FDI inflows at ~$27.6-28 billion (15th globally, essentially flat/down slightly from $28.1B in 2023), while China's 2024 FDI inflows were $116 billion (4th globally, down 29% from $163B in 2023 but still ~4x India's total). Even India's own generous domestic accounting (DPIIT), which uses a broader methodology and India's fiscal year (Apr 2024-Mar 2025), shows $81.04 billion — a genuine record for India, but still well short of China's $116B for calendar 2024. The only metric where India plausibly outperformed China in 2024 is a narrower, different measure — fDi Markets/Financial Times greenfield-project announcement/pipeline data (India led on announced greenfield project capex/count as China's project activity fell) — but that is investment-pipeline/announcement data, not realized 'FDI inflows,' and conflating the two is the apparent source of this event's claim. Since the title and description specifically assert India surpassed China in actual FDI inflows, and every inflow-basis dataset found (UNCTAD, OECD-referenced, DPIIT) shows China's inflows remained several times larger than India's in 2024, the claim as stated is false. Country and year are otherwise correctly matched to genuine underlying trends (China's FDI decline, India's rising FDI/manufacturing narrative), so this is a case of a real backdrop being overstated into a false headline claim rather than a wrong-year event.

verifications.reason: By the standard, internationally-recognized measure of FDI inflows (UNCTAD's World Investment Report 2025, BoP-based), China received USD 116 billion in FDI in 2024 (ranked 4th globally, down 29% from $163B in 2023) versus India's USD 27.6 billion (ranked 15th globally, itself down 1.9% from $28.1B in 2023) — China took in more than 4x India's inflows, the opposite of 'surpassing.' India's inflows were not a record either: World Bank/UNCTAD data show a slight year-on-year decline, and on India's own domestic fiscal-year accounting (FY2024-25), while gross FDI equity inflows rose 14% to $81B (a 3-year high, not an all-time record), NET FDI collapsed ~96% to just $0.35B — the lowest level in at least two decades — due to record repatriation/divestment ($51.5B) and a jump in outward FDI. The only place India plausibly outpaced China in 2024 was in a narrower, non-standard metric — announced greenfield project capital expenditure (India's committed greenfield capex rose to ~$110B, making it the 3rd-largest global recipient of greenfield project announcements) — but that is forward-looking committed investment, not realized 'FDI inflows,' and no mainstream source frames it as India 'surpassing China in FDI inflows.' The core factual claim as stated does not hold under the primary measure; if anything the data show the reverse for actual inflows.

Multiple independent 2024/2025 sources (UNCTAD World Investment Report 2025 data as reported by fDi Intelligence/fDi Markets, Business Standard, FT Locations, India Business Trade) confirm the hedged claim "surpassing China in some measures." On the headline UNCTAD balance-of-payments FDI inflow figure, China ($116bn, rank 4) still exceeded India ($27.6bn, rank 15) in 2024 — so India did NOT surpass China on that single aggregate measure. However, on greenfield-investment measures — the metric most tied to the "China+1 manufacturing/tech diversification" narrative in the description — India clearly surpassed China in 2024: India became the 2nd/3rd-largest global recipient of greenfield FDI project capital expenditure (~$108-110bn, up >25%, surpassing Germany and the UK), while China's inbound FDI fell 29% for a second straight year and its greenfield project growth fell 10%. FT Locations explicitly states "India emerged as the main recipient in Asia in terms of international private equity investment, followed by China," and multiple outlets frame 2024 as the year India's greenfield/manufacturing FDI activity outpaced China's amid China+1 diversification. Given the description's own hedge ("in some measures," not "overall FDI"), this matches the documented, multiply-corroborated reality for calendar year 2024. Country and year confirmed correct.

The underlying 2024 trend is real — China's FDI collapsed sharply (China+1 diversification, capital flight) while India remained relatively resilient — but the two specific claims in the description don't hold up against the primary/standard sources. (1) "Record FDI inflows": false. India's FY2024-25 FDI was $81.04B (DPIIT/PIB), up 14% YoY, but this is BELOW India's actual all-time record of $83.57-84.83B set in FY2021-22 — so 2024 was a multi-year high, not a record. (2) "Surpassing China": true only on one narrow technical measure, false on the standard/primary one. On the World Bank/IMF net-FDI-inflows (BoP) indicator, India ($27.14B, 2024) did exceed China ($18.56B, 2024) — a real, checkable data point, driven mainly by China's record capital outflow rather than an India surge. But on the measure the world actually uses to rank countries' FDI attractiveness — UNCTAD's World Investment Report 2025 — China remained far ahead of India in 2024: China ranked 4th globally with ~$116B in inflows (down 29% from $163B in 2023) versus India ranked 15th with ~$28B (essentially flat YoY). So on the headline/standard comparison, China still dwarfed India roughly 4-to-1; India did not "surpass" China in any broadly reported sense. Country and year are correct and a real, related 2024 phenomenon occurred, but "record" is wrong and "surpassing China" only survives on a cherry-picked/obscure metric, not the mainstream one — a material magnitude/scope miss.
